title: DR1 accepts document files up to 50MB; the frontend refuses anything over 10 MB.

finding.frontend: The file question's hint reads "Your file must be:" over the bullet "smaller than 10 MB", and the same 10 MB is enforced twice — in the browser, from the data-max-file-size attribute on the form, and on the server, where an oversize upload is answered with "The selected file must be smaller than 10 MB" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-52). The constant is deliberate rather than arbitrary: the comment above it records that 10 MB decimal was chosen to sit clear of the CDP nginx ingress cap of 10 MiB.
finding.prototype: DR1's file requirements list opens with "files that are smaller than 50MB" (app/views/upload-documents.html:165-170) — five times the frontend's ceiling, and the first thing the trader reads about their file.
finding.difference: Raise the accepted file size to 50MB. It is one frontend constant: MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB in upload-config.js feeds the hint bullet, the data-max-file-size attribute the browser check reads, the hapi route's payload maxBytes, the server-side size check and the oversize error's own wording, so all five move together when the number does. Nothing has to land first — the backend already accepts a file this size, and takes its per-upload ceiling from whatever the frontend sends it. The one thing to settle before the copy changes is the platform: a comment beside the constant records a CDP nginx ingress cap of 10 MiB, and if that cap is real and unchanged a 50MB file will be refused at the edge before the application sees it. Confirm the ingress limit with the platform team and raise it in the same piece of work, because a hint promising 50MB over an ingress that refuses it is worse than the honest 10 MB.
finding.falsifiedBy: Uploading a file between 10 MB and 50MB through the frontend and having it accepted.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both hints, then followed the 10 MB through the whole upload path because the band turned on whether the number is a frontend constant. It is. MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB = 10 at upload-config.js:42 is the sole source: MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES and MAX_FILE_SIZE_LABEL derive from it (:44-45), the label reaches the hint and the attribute through render.js:54-55 (confirmed as data-max-file-size="10000000" and the bullet "smaller than 10 MB" in both frontend captures), OVERSIZE_FILE_MESSAGE is built from the same label (:46) and appears in the DOM as data-oversize-error="The selected file must be smaller than 10 MB", MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES caps the hapi route (controller.js:311) and exceedsMaxFileSize guards the handler (form/errors.js:34). DR1's "files that are smaller than 50MB" is the first bullet in the captured requirements list. Both sides of the claim are exactly as stated. The band did not survive, see correction.
finding.correction: Banded needs-backend on the reasoning that "the ingress cap and the upload service's own limit have to be raised first". Re-banded frontend-work. The band table reserves needs-backend for an API, contract or persistence change that has to land first, and there is none here. The backend is already sized for this: spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size is 50MB and max-request-size 51MB, and cdp.uploader.max-file-size is 52428800 bytes — 50 MiB (trade-imports-animals-backend src/main/resources/application.yml:29-30, :45), every one of them env-overridable. Nor does the backend hold a limit of its own to raise: the frontend passes maxFileSize down with each upload it initiates (documents/handlers/reads/download.js:36 into services/document-uploads/real.js:26,38), so the backend is currently being told 10 MB by the very constant this finding changes. What remains is the platform, not the backend, and it rests on a single unverifiable source: the CDP nginx ingress 10 MiB cap appears nowhere in either repository except the comment at upload-config.js:40-41 — no manifest, no chart, no environment variable, nothing corroborating. That is a pre-flight check to make, not a dependency to schedule behind, so it has been moved out of the band and into the difference slot as the one thing to confirm.

relatedTo.why: both rewrite the same four-line file requirements list
